title: Injective module sheaves have vanishing Cech cohomology on a ringed site
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in J}$ be any covering in $\mathcal C$. For the underlying abelian sheaf $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$, the Cech complex [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,I_{\mathrm{ab}})=\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in J^{p+1}} I(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U U_{i_p})$ with its alternating restriction differential has $\check H^p(\mathcal U,I_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every $p>0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FC (lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech), via Lemmas 03FB and 03AT, and the underlying-abelian identification in Lemma 03FD

proof.text: Write $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$ for presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. The sheafification functor is an exact left adjoint to the inclusion of sheaves, so an injective sheaf $I$ is injective in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-injective-module-injective-presheaf].

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FB and the first sentence of Lemma Tag 03FC

proof.text: For the covering $\mathcal U$, form the free presheaf complex $K_\bullet$ whose degree-$p$ term is the direct sum of the representable free module presheaves on $U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}$ and whose differential is the alternating sum of the face maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-free-cech-complex-exact], $K_\bullet$ is exact in positive degrees. The proof is the decomposition at each object $W$ and each map $W\to U$ into the free-module complex on the set of lifts of that map, contracted by adjoining one chosen lift; the empty lift set contributes the zero complex.

For every presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $G$, the Yoneda identification $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_V,G)\cong G(V)$, $\beta\mapsto\beta_V(e_{\mathrm{id}_V})$, of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] (whose inverse sends $s$ to $e_\varphi\mapsto s|_\varphi$) and the direct-sum/product adjunction identify the cochain complex $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)}(K_\bullet,G)$ with the Čech complex $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,G)$: precomposition by a face map is restriction along the corresponding projection, so the differential is the alternating restriction differential.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AS (lemma-cech-map-into) and the proof of Tag 03FC

proof.text: Since $I$ is injective in the presheaf category by Step 1, the contravariant functor $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ is exact. Applying it to the positive-degree exact complex $K_\bullet$ from Step 2 gives $H^p(\operatorname{Hom}(K_\bullet,I))=0$ for every $p>0$; Step 3 identifies this with $\check H^p(\mathcal U,I)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FC (lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech), proof after Tags 03FB and 03F5

proof.text: The underlying abelian presheaf $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the same sections and restriction maps as $I$, so its Čech complex is the same complex of abelian groups. Therefore $\check H^p(\mathcal U,I_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every $p>0$.
